bounded_statement: The report's selected inferential result (Pearson chi-squared test of independence on 120 sample rows: chi-squared = 20.0000, df = 2, p = 4.540e-05, Cramer's V = 0.408) enters each of the 30 monitoring wells four times (once per visit) into a procedure that assumes each tallied row is an independent observation, even though the data description designates well_id as the independent unit and coastal_zone is a fixed well-level property. Exceedances cluster strongly within wells, and collapsing to one entry per well (any-exceedance per well: dune ridge 3/10, back barrier 6/10, tidal flat 8/10) yields chi-squared of approximately 5.2 with df = 2 and p of approximately 0.076, which is not significant at conventional levels. The reported significance therefore depends on the repeated per-well entries and is not supported at the authorized independent-unit level; the descriptive rate gradient itself (0.250/0.500/0.750) remains a valid summary of the samples.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses the clustered design (30 wells, 4 visits each), so the repeated-entry structure is not concealed; however, disclosure does not make the chi-squared p-value valid at the row level.

source_refs.quoted_text:
def contingency(rows):
    """Zone-by-exceedance counts, one sample row per tallied observation."""
    counts = np.zeros((len(ZONES), 2), dtype=int)
    for row in rows:
        zone_ix = ZONES.index(row["coastal_zone"])
        col = 0 if row["chloride_mg_l"] >= LIMIT_MG_L else 1
        counts[zone_ix, col] += 1
    return counts

evidence.description: The input data shows strong within-well clustering of exceedance status, so the four rows per well are not exchangeable with independent observations; for example every one of DR09's four samples exceeds the 250 mg/L limit while many wells have none.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to show the repeated per-well entries are inconsequential by re-running the inference at the authorized unit level. First I verified the reported numbers from the raw data: the 3x2 table is (10,30)/(20,20)/(30,10), giving chi-squared = 400/20 = 20.0 exactly, df = 2, p = 4.54e-05, Cramer's V = sqrt(20/120) = 0.408, matching the report. Then I collapsed to one entry per well. Classifying each well by whether any of its four samples exceeded 250 mg/L gives 3/10 (dune ridge: DR08, DR09, DR10), 6/10 (back barrier: BB05-BB10), 8/10 (tidal flat: TF03-TF10); the chi-squared statistic on this 30-well table is approximately 5.16 with df = 2 and p of approximately 0.076. An alternative majority-of-visits classification (3, 5, 8 wells) gives chi-squared of approximately 5.09, p of approximately 0.078. Under either well-level summary the association is not significant at the 0.05 level, so the falsification failed: the reported significance depends materially on entering each well four times. I also checked whether within-well responses looked effectively independent (which would mitigate the concern) and found the opposite: exceedances are concentrated in specific wells, with many wells showing all four or zero exceedances.

root_cause: The contingency() function in workflow/analysis.py tallies every sample row as one observation ('one sample row per tallied observation') into the zone-by-exceedance table, and main() passes that table to scipy.stats.chi2_contingency, whose p-value calculation assumes independent observations. Because each well was visited four times and coastal_zone is constant within a well, each independent unit (well_id) is counted four times, quadruplicating the effective sample size (120 rows versus 30 independent wells) and inflating the chi-squared statistic and shrinking the p-value relative to a well-level analysis.
